source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-272521:Shears item use statistic ignores tool component
source_meta._title: Statistic for using shears doesn't increase when mining certain blocks

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.4 (an affected stable release explicitly listed in the report)
stor.environment: A new single-player Java Edition world using the integrated server. Use Survival mode for the actual mining action. Enable cheats for deterministic setup commands, and use a Superflat world so the carpet can be placed on a predictable level surface.
preconditions: Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.4 is installed and selected in the launcher.
The test world permits commands because the report requires two /scoreboard commands; cheats should therefore be enabled when the world is created.
The same player must execute the scoreboard commands and perform the shears mining action.
Use the default Attack/Destroy control (left mouse button), or identify the rebound control before testing.
Do not use the test shears after resetting the score to 0 until the carpet is mined in the trigger step.

steps.action: Start the exact affected Minecraft version selected for this reproduction.
steps.exact_input: Launch Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.4 from the Minecraft Launcher.
steps.success_cue: The main menu displays Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.4.

steps.action: Create a simple command-enabled test world. From the main menu, choose Singleplayer and Create New World. Set the game mode to Survival, enable cheats, select the Superflat world type, and create the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Survival; Allow Cheats: ON; World Type: Superflat -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player spawns in a flat world with the Survival HUD visible, including hearts and hunger icons.

steps.action: Wait for the integrated server and nearby chunks to finish loading before entering commands.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, player movement responds normally, and opening chat does not stall.

steps.action: Create the statistic-backed scoreboard objective specified by the report. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that the objective named "shear" was created, with no red syntax or permission error.

steps.action: Display the new objective in the sidebar. Open chat with T, enter the command exactly, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A scoreboard sidebar headed "shear" appears on the right side of the screen. The player may not have an entry yet because no score has been initialized.

steps.action: Obtain one fresh pair of shears without performing an unrelated shearing action. Open chat, run the give command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A shears item is present in the player's hotbar or inventory and has a full durability bar/no visible durability damage.

steps.action: Create the carpet target on the flat ground next to the player. Stand still on the level surface, open chat, execute the setblock command, and press Enter. The relative coordinates place the carpet one block in the positive-X direction from the block containing the player.
steps.success_cue: One white carpet block is visible on top of the ground immediately beside the player.

steps.action: Explicitly restore or confirm the report-required game mode after command-based setup. Open chat, execute the game-mode command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms Survival mode, and the Survival hearts and hunger HUD is visible.

steps.action: Ensure the shears are in the nine-slot hotbar. If they are only in the main inventory, press E, move the shears into an empty hotbar slot, and close the inventory with E.
steps.exact_input: E; move minecraft:shears to a hotbar slot if necessary; E
steps.success_cue: The shears icon is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the shears using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: Press the number key corresponding to the shears hotbar slot, or scroll until that slot is highlighted.
steps.success_cue: The shears slot has the active-slot highlight and the shears model is visible in the player's main hand.

steps.action: Initialize a visible baseline immediately before the test. Without using the shears on anything, press T, enter the scoreboard command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The sidebar displays the executing player's name with a score of 0 under the "shear" objective, and the shears remain selected.

steps.action: Face the adjacent white carpet and place the crosshair directly over its thin top surface. Do not press the Attack/Destroy control yet.
steps.exact_input: Move and aim with the mouse until the crosshair targets minecraft:white_carpet.
steps.success_cue: The white carpet is within mining reach, is under the crosshair, and the shears remain visible in the main hand.

steps.action: Mine the targeted white carpet while continuing to hold the shears. Press the Attack/Destroy control and stop as soon as the one carpet block has broken; do not use the shears again.
steps.exact_input: Attack/Destroy (default: press or hold the left mouse button until the carpet breaks)
steps.success_cue: The targeted white carpet block has disappeared and, unless immediately collected, its dropped carpet item is visible at that position. No additional block or entity has been acted upon with the shears.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just destroyed exactly one white carpet block in Survival mode with the selected shears. The "shear" statistic objective remains displayed in the sidebar, and no further shears interaction has occurred. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus multiplayer, world seed, terrain type, carpet color, or an exact target location. A new single-player Superflat world and white carpet are deterministic practical choices that preserve the stated test condition.
The report does not provide formal numbered Steps to Reproduce. The procedure is reconstructed from its description and exact scoreboard commands.

The report also identifies tall grass, large fern, seagrass, tall seagrass, and nether sprouts as affected targets. This plan uses carpet because it is the report's primary example and requires no dimension travel, water placement, biome search, or multi-block plant setup. Those other blocks would require separate runs and target-specific setup.
The baseline command that sets the player's objective score to 0 is not stated in the report; it is included to ensure the sidebar has an unambiguous visible pre-trigger value.
The supplied attachment files were not available as content in the report text and were not used to add reproduction requirements.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-273932:"Times Used" statistic for watter bottles increases by 2 when converting dirt to mud in creative
source_meta._title: "minecraft.used:minecraft.potion" increases by a value of two when using water bottles to create mud in creative mode

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.4, the latest full release explicitly listed as affected in the report
stor.environment: A fresh single-player Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.4 world running in Creative mode with commands available. No particular seed, coordinates, difficulty, world type, graphics setting, dedicated server, or additional player is specified by the report. Instructions name default keyboard and mouse controls; use the equivalent bound control if they have been changed.
preconditions: Select and launch the exact Java Edition 1.21.4 installation rather than a fix version such as snapshot 25w36a or a later version.

Use a fresh world so that a scoreboard objective named UseWaterBottle does not already exist. If reusing a world, remove or rename any existing objective with that exact case-sensitive name before beginning.
Create the world in Creative mode and ensure commands are available. A world created directly in Creative mode satisfies the report's requirement to switch into Creative mode.
Have an ordinary mouse interaction available for the Use Item/Place Block action, which is right-click by default.
Do not use any potion or water bottle after initializing the scoreboard baseline and before the designated trigger step.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.4. From the title screen, select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and create the world. The seed and world type may remain at their defaults because the report does not specify them. Wait until surrounding terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded world in Creative mode; the Creative hotbar is visible and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Create the scoreboard objective from in-game chat. Press T to open chat, enter the supplied command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that the new objective UseWaterBottle was created. No red command error is shown.

steps.action: Display the new objective in the sidebar. Press T, enter the supplied command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A scoreboard headed UseWaterBottle is assigned to the right-side sidebar, although the player may not yet have a visible score entry.

steps.action: Initialize the current player's score to a visible zero baseline. Press T, enter the command with the leading slash, and press Enter. This added setup command makes the amount changed by the single trigger interaction unambiguous.
steps.success_cue: The sidebar shows the current player's name with a score of 0 under UseWaterBottle.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, identifiable by its compass icon. Click the search field and type the exact search text. Locate the item whose tooltip is Dirt, then left-click or drag it into an empty hotbar slot at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A Dirt stack is present in a known hotbar slot.

steps.action: While the Creative inventory remains open, click the search field, press Ctrl+A to select the previous search text, and replace it with the exact search text. Locate the potion item whose tooltip/display name is Water Bottle, not another potion, and place it into a different empty hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A Water Bottle is present in the hotbar, separately from the Dirt stack.

steps.action: Press E or Esc to close the Creative inventory. Select the hotbar slot containing Dirt by pressing its corresponding number key or using the mouse wheel until that slot is highlighted.
steps.success_cue: The Dirt slot is highlighted in the hotbar and the player is visibly holding Dirt.

steps.action: Find an existing solid ground block with empty space directly above it. Aim the crosshair at its upper face and perform Use Item/Place Block once, which is right-click by default, to place the Dirt block.
steps.success_cue: A distinct Dirt block has been placed in the world within the player's interaction reach.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Water Bottle by pressing its corresponding number key or using the mouse wheel until that slot is highlighted.
steps.success_cue: The Water Bottle slot is highlighted and the player is visibly holding a Water Bottle.

steps.action: Position the player within normal interaction reach of the Dirt block placed in step 8. Aim the center crosshair directly at any visible face of that specific Dirt block. Do not use the bottle yet.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair rests on the placed Dirt block while the Water Bottle remains selected and the sidebar baseline still reads 0.

steps.action: Perform Use Item/Place Block exactly once—right-click by default—while continuing to target the placed Dirt block with the Water Bottle. Release the mouse button immediately and do not click a second time.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one water-bottle use interaction has just been completed against the targeted Dirt block; no additional bottle-use input has been made.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just used the selected Water Bottle exactly once on the placed Dirt block in Creative mode, with UseWaterBottle initialized to 0 and displayed in the sidebar. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately, before performing any additional item-use interaction or changing the score.
uncertainties: The report lists numerous affected versions rather than mandating one specific test version. Java Edition 1.21.4 is selected because it is the latest full release explicitly listed as affected.
The report does not specify a seed, coordinates, world type, difficulty, multiplayer environment, or graphics configuration; none are added as reproduction requirements.
The command that initializes UseWaterBottle to 0 is not included in the report. It is an execution aid added to provide a deterministic visible baseline before the single trigger interaction.

Default controls are referenced for clarity. Rebound controls should use the actions named Open Inventory, Open Chat, and Use Item/Place Block rather than relying exclusively on the stated default keys.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-302587:“minecraft.used:minecraft.ITEM” doesn't increase when placing items onto shelves
source_meta._title: minecraft.used:minecraft.BOOK_TYPE doesn't increase when placing books onto chiseled bookshelves

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 22w45a, the latest snapshot listed as affected in the report. Do not perform the reproduction in 1.19.3 Pre-release 1, which the report lists as the fix version.
stor.environment: Fresh single-player Java Edition 22w45a world. Use Creative mode with commands enabled as a practical execution choice. Enable the built-in Update 1.20 experimental data pack during world creation so the Chiseled Bookshelf is available. No seed, coordinates, dedicated server, or multiple players are required by the report.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can start the historical Java Edition snapshot 22w45a.
Create a new world rather than reusing an existing world, because the required Update 1.20 experimental feature toggle is selected during world creation.
Use Creative mode so the required Lectern, Chiseled Bookshelf, and Book and Quill can be obtained deterministically without crafting.
Commands must be enabled because the reproduction uses two /scoreboard commands.
Use the default Use Item/Place Block input of right-click, or the equivalent rebound control.
Keep the sidebar visible throughout the lectern control interaction and the final chiseled-bookshelf interaction.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft: Java Edition using the 22w45a snapshot installation. On the main menu, verify that the displayed game version is 22w45a before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 22w45a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and ensure Allow Cheats is ON. The world name and seed may be left at their defaults because the report supplies neither a seed nor coordinates.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is configured for Creative mode with commands permitted.

steps.action: Before creating the world, open the Data Packs screen. Move the built-in data pack identified as Update 1.20 from the available list to the selected/enabled list, then choose Done. Accept the experimental-feature warning if one appears.
steps.exact_input: Create New World -> Data Packs -> enable the built-in Update 1.20 data pack -> Done
steps.success_cue: The Update 1.20 built-in data pack is shown as selected, and the world-creation screen indicates or warns that experimental settings are enabled.

steps.action: Choose Create New World and wait until world generation and chunk loading finish. Do not begin setup while the loading screen is present.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the world, nearby terrain has rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the report's objective-creation command exactly as written, including the leading slash, then press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that the scoreboard objective UseWritableBook was created successfully; no red command error is shown.

steps.action: Press T to open chat again. Enter the report's sidebar-display command exactly as written, including the leading slash, then press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A scoreboard sidebar titled UseWritableBook is visible on the right side of the game screen. The player may not have a listed score until the tracked item is first used.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, identified by a magnifying-glass icon. Search for and move one Lectern, one Chiseled Bookshelf, and one Book and Quill into separate hotbar slots. The hotbar is the nine-slot row shown at the bottom of the screen during play. In commands and statistics, the Book and Quill is the writable_book item referenced by the report.
steps.exact_input: Search terms: Lectern; Chiseled Bookshelf; Book and Quill
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a Lectern, a Chiseled Bookshelf, and a Book and Quill.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E. Select the Lectern's hotbar slot using the corresponding number key or mouse wheel. Aim at the top surface of a nearby solid ground block and use right-click to place the Lectern.
steps.exact_input: Select Lectern -> right-click a ground block
steps.success_cue: A Lectern is placed in front of the player and can be reached without moving far away.

steps.action: Select the Chiseled Bookshelf's hotbar slot. Aim at the top surface of another ground block close to, but not replacing or obstructing, the Lectern. Right-click to place the Chiseled Bookshelf while facing the intended accessible side.
steps.exact_input: Select Chiseled Bookshelf -> right-click a nearby ground block
steps.success_cue: An empty Chiseled Bookshelf is placed near the Lectern, with its shelf-patterned front face visible and reachable by the player.

steps.action: Select the Book and Quill in the hotbar. Confirm that it is the active slot by checking that its icon is outlined in the hotbar and the item appears in the player's hand.
steps.exact_input: Select the hotbar slot containing Book and Quill
steps.success_cue: The Book and Quill is held in the player's active hand.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair directly at the Lectern and use right-click once to place the Book and Quill onto it. If the lectern reading interface opens automatically, leave it open for the removal step after recording the sidebar value.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the empty Lectern while holding the Book and Quill
steps.success_cue: The Lectern visibly contains the book, and the Book and Quill is no longer held in the player's hand; the lectern reading interface may be open.

steps.action: Read the UseWritableBook sidebar and record the exact numeric score now displayed beside the player's name. This is the control value produced after using the Book and Quill on the Lectern; do not proceed until a numeric player entry is visible.
steps.success_cue: The player's numeric UseWritableBook score is visible and has been recorded for later comparison.

steps.action: Retrieve the Book and Quill from the Lectern. If the lectern reading interface is already open, click its Take Book button. Otherwise, right-click the occupied Lectern to open the reading interface and then click Take Book.
steps.exact_input: Occupied Lectern -> right-click if necessary -> Take Book
steps.success_cue: The Lectern is visibly empty and the Book and Quill has returned to the player's inventory or cursor.

steps.action: If the retrieved Book and Quill is not already in a hotbar slot, press E, move it into an empty hotbar slot, and close the inventory. Select that slot so the Book and Quill is held again.
steps.exact_input: Select the hotbar slot containing Book and Quill
steps.success_cue: The same type of writable item, Book and Quill, is held in the active hand and is ready for use on the Chiseled Bookshelf.

steps.action: Stand close enough to interact with the Chiseled Bookshelf. Aim at the shelf-patterned front face rather than its side, top, or a neighboring block. Confirm visually that the bookshelf is still empty and that the UseWritableBook sidebar remains visible.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is on the empty front face of the Chiseled Bookshelf, the Book and Quill is held, and the scoreboard sidebar is visible.

steps.action: Record the exact UseWritableBook score displayed immediately before the bookshelf interaction. Without performing any additional item-use action, right-click the front face of the empty Chiseled Bookshelf once while holding the Book and Quill.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the front face of the empty Chiseled Bookshelf while holding the Book and Quill
steps.success_cue: One Book and Quill has been inserted into the Chiseled Bookshelf and the single interaction has completed; do not perform another interaction before handing off.

stor.handoff_condition: The Book and Quill has just been inserted into the previously empty Chiseled Bookshelf with one right-click, the pre-interaction UseWritableBook score has been recorded, and the UseWritableBook sidebar remains visible. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately, before removing the book or using another item.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, server type, or multiplayer requirement. A fresh single-player Creative world with commands enabled is used as the simplest deterministic execution path.

The Chiseled Bookshelf is an experimental Update 1.20 feature in the affected snapshots and therefore requires the built-in Update 1.20 data pack to be enabled during world creation, although the report does not explicitly mention this setup requirement.
The report uses both the spelling 'writeable book' and the display name 'book and quill.' The exact tracked item is preserved from its command criterion: minecraft:writable_book.

The report does not explicitly state whether the identical item instance must be moved from the Lectern to the Chiseled Bookshelf. This plan retrieves and reuses the Book and Quill to follow the stated order as closely as possible.

The exact capitalization or presentation of the built-in Update 1.20 data pack label may vary with language settings, but it is the built-in pack that enables the 1.20 experimental features, including the Chiseled Bookshelf.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-277152:The statistic for killing a creaking doesn't increment when breaking a creaking heart
source_meta._title: The statistics screen does not visually differentiate the creaking and creaking_transient entities

stor.environment: A fresh single-player Java Edition 24w40a world in the Overworld, with the Winter Drop experiment enabled. Use Creative mode with commands/cheats available as a practical way to obtain the experimental blocks and execute the report's commands. Keep the fresh world's default doMobSpawning gamerule enabled.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to make historical Java Edition snapshots available, and select snapshot 24w40a.
Use a newly created world so the player's mob-kill statistics do not contain results from earlier testing.
Enable the Winter Drop experiment while creating the world; the creaking, pale oak log, and creaking heart content in 24w40a is behind this experiment.

Use Creative mode and enable commands/cheats. Creative mode is not stated as a bug requirement, but it provides deterministic access to the required blocks, while commands/cheats are required for the supplied /summon, /time, and /damage commands.
Remain in the Overworld. No seed or coordinates are specified.
Leave the doMobSpawning gamerule at its fresh-world default value of true so the creaking heart can spawn its creaking.
Use an open, solid, approximately level area with free space around and above the planned three-block log-and-heart column.
The instructions name default keyboard and mouse inputs. If controls have been rebound, use the bound input for the same action.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft: Java Edition using snapshot 24w40a. At the title screen, verify that the displayed version is 24w40a before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Java Edition title screen is open and identifies the running version as 24w40a.

steps.action: Open the single-player world creation screen by selecting Singleplayer and then Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Set the new world's game mode to Creative. Ensure commands are available; Creative single-player worlds normally provide command access, but enable Allow Commands/Cheats if the creation screen exposes a separate option.
steps.success_cue: The world is configured for Creative mode and will permit in-game commands.

steps.action: Open the world-creation options containing experimental features, normally More -> Experiments in this version.
steps.success_cue: The Experiments screen is visible and lists the available experimental feature toggles.

steps.action: Turn the Winter Drop experiment on. Confirm any warning that experimental features may make the world unstable, then return to the main world-creation screen.
steps.success_cue: Winter Drop is shown as enabled for the new world.

steps.action: Create the world and wait until terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the loaded Overworld, can move normally, and can execute commands.

steps.action: Locate a nearby open, solid, approximately level area. Choose a position with at least two empty blocks above the ground for a vertical pale-oak-log, creaking-heart, pale-oak-log column, plus unobstructed ground around it where an entity can appear.
steps.success_cue: A clear construction position and surrounding spawn area are available in loaded chunks.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory action, whose default key is E, and open the Search Items tab, normally represented by a compass icon.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open with an item search field available.

steps.action: Search for Pale Oak Log. Pick up a stack of the block and place it into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine slots at the bottom of the inventory and gameplay screen.
steps.success_cue: At least two Pale Oak Logs are present in one of the player's hotbar slots.

steps.action: Clear or select all text in the Creative search field, search for Creaking Heart, and place one Creaking Heart into a different hotbar slot. Close the inventory using E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed, and the hotbar contains both Pale Oak Logs and a Creaking Heart.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so the player is not holding a block while killing the first creaking. Select a hotbar slot with the corresponding number key or mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: The active hotbar slot is empty and the player's hand is empty.

steps.action: Open in-game chat using the chat action, whose default key is T.
steps.success_cue: The chat command input field is open.

steps.action: Enter the report's summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and a command-spawned creaking exists at or immediately beside the player's position.

steps.action: Move approximately two or three blocks away from the summoned creaking, then turn toward it so it is visible and within melee reach when approached. Do not leave the area.
steps.success_cue: The command-spawned creaking is clearly visible and can be approached for a direct player attack.

steps.action: Approach within attack range, place the crosshair on the creaking, and use the attack action, whose default input is left-click, to kill it. A command- or spawn-egg-created creaking in this affected version has only one health point, so one direct player attack should be sufficient.
steps.success_cue: The creaking has entered its death/removal sequence as a result of the player's direct attack.

steps.action: Wait until the first creaking's death animation has finished and the entity is no longer present before constructing the heart setup.
steps.success_cue: The first creaking has completely disappeared, leaving no command-spawned creaking alive nearby.

steps.action: Return to the clear construction position and select the hotbar slot containing Pale Oak Logs.
steps.success_cue: Pale Oak Log is displayed as the item held in the player's hand.

steps.action: Place one Pale Oak Log on the chosen ground block by aiming at the ground's top face and using the place/use action, whose default input is right-click. Placing against a top face makes the log's axis vertical.
steps.success_cue: One upright Pale Oak Log occupies the bottom position of the planned three-block column.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Creaking Heart.
steps.success_cue: Creaking Heart is displayed as the item held in the player's hand.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of the bottom Pale Oak Log and place the Creaking Heart on top of it using the place/use action.
steps.success_cue: The Creaking Heart is directly above and touching the bottom Pale Oak Log.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing Pale Oak Logs again.
steps.success_cue: Pale Oak Log is displayed as the item held in the player's hand.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of the Creaking Heart and place a second Pale Oak Log on top using the place/use action. The result must be a vertical three-block column ordered Pale Oak Log, Creaking Heart, Pale Oak Log from bottom to top. All three blocks must be aligned along the same vertical axis.
steps.success_cue: A vertical log-heart-log column is complete, with the Creaking Heart directly between two vertically aligned Pale Oak Logs.

steps.action: Open in-game chat using the chat action, whose default key is T.
steps.success_cue: The chat command input field is open.

steps.action: Enter the report's time command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and the Overworld has changed to nighttime while the aligned heart structure remains loaded.

steps.action: Stand near the column without leaving the loaded area and wait for the active Creaking Heart to spawn a creaking. Keep the surrounding ground in view by slowly scanning the area, but do not break or replace any part of the column. Continue only after a creaking has visibly appeared nearby.
steps.success_cue: A heart-spawned creaking is visible near the aligned Creaking Heart structure.

steps.action: Open in-game chat using the chat action, whose default key is T. Do this while the heart-spawned creaking still exists.
steps.success_cue: The chat command input field is open and the heart-spawned creaking remains present.

steps.action: Enter the report's damage command exactly as written, including the leading slash, selector, entity identifier, damage amount, damage type, and source attribution, then press Enter. Execute it from in-game chat as the same player whose statistics will be inspected.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and targets the nearest minecraft:creaking_transient entity, with the executing player specified as the damage source.

steps.action: Wait until the targeted heart-spawned creaking finishes its death/removal sequence. Do not run another summon or damage command.
steps.success_cue: The targeted heart-spawned creaking is no longer present, and both kill actions have been completed once.

steps.action: Open the pause menu using the menu action, whose default key is Esc.
steps.success_cue: The pause menu is open.

steps.action: Select the Statistics button in the pause menu.
steps.success_cue: The Statistics screen is open and its statistics-category controls are visible.

steps.action: Select the Mobs category or tab in the Statistics screen.
steps.success_cue: The mob statistics list is open.

steps.action: Scroll through the mob statistics list until both entries corresponding to the two creaking entity types are simultaneously visible. Stop interacting as soon as the two Creaking-labeled statistic entries are in view.
steps.exact_input: mouse wheel or statistics-screen scroll control
steps.success_cue: The Mobs statistics screen is open with both Creaking statistic entries visible and ready for visual inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The player's Mobs statistics screen is open immediately after one player-attributed command-spawned creaking kill and one player-attributed creaking_transient kill, and both Creaking statistic entries are visible. Hand control to the observation subsystem without clicking, scrolling, closing the screen, or otherwise changing the displayed entries.
uncertainties: The report affects both 24w40a and 1.21.3. Snapshot 24w40a is recommended because it directly matches the report's requirement to enable the Winter Drop experiment and was the version current when the report was created.

The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is used only as a deterministic implementation choice for obtaining Pale Oak Logs and a Creaking Heart; commands/cheats are necessary for the supplied commands.
No seed, coordinates, biome, or precise construction location is supplied. The report supports using any suitable loaded Overworld area.

The report says the Pale Oak Logs must be correctly aligned but does not describe the placement geometry. External version-relevant documentation establishes that the heart and both logs must share one axis; a vertical log-heart-log column is the simplest practical arrangement.

The exact delay and position at which the Creaking Heart spawns its creaking are not specified and may vary. The executor must wait for the entity itself to become visible rather than relying on a fixed delay.

The exact placement of the Experiments button within the 24w40a world-creation screen is not stated in the report; the More -> Experiments path is an operational UI inference. The essential report condition is that Winter Drop is enabled before world creation.

The report does not explicitly state the doMobSpawning gamerule, but a heart-spawned creaking requires mob spawning to remain enabled. A fresh world normally satisfies this without an additional command.

source_meta._title: "minecraft.used:minecraft.trident" doesn't increase when throwing a trident

stor.environment: A fresh single-player Java Edition 1.21.3 world in Survival mode with commands/cheats enabled. Use one player, default or known controls, and an unenchanted trident. No specific seed, coordinates, difficulty, server configuration, or graphics settings are stated in the report.
preconditions: Launch the affected Java Edition release 1.21.3, not the unaffected comparison version 1.21.1.

Use a fresh world or a player profile in that world that has not previously used a trident, so the initial trident-use statistic is not confused with earlier throws. This is a deterministic test choice rather than a report-stated requirement.
Enable commands/cheats so the two supplied scoreboard commands and the deterministic item-give command can be executed.
Ensure the player has at least one empty inventory or hotbar slot.
The test trident must not have the Riptide enchantment.
Perform exactly one trident throw before inspecting the configured objective and Items statistics; do not use the trident for melee attacks or make additional throws.

steps.action: Open or create the single-player Survival world with commands enabled. After spawning, wait until nearby terrain is rendered and movement and chat input respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded Java Edition 1.21.3 world, can move normally, and has permission to execute commands.

steps.action: Move to an open area and face a direction where a thrown trident will not immediately strike a nearby wall, entity, or block directly in front of the player.
steps.success_cue: There is clear space in front of the crosshair for the trident projectile to leave the player's hand visibly.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the report's first scoreboard command with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that the scoreboard objective named MC-278071 was created. If the command reports that the objective already exists, use a fresh world or remove the old objective before restarting the procedure.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat again, enter the report's sidebar-display command with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A scoreboard sidebar headed MC-278071 is displayed on the right side of the gameplay HUD; the player list beneath the heading may initially be empty.

steps.action: Obtain one deterministic, plain trident by opening chat with T, entering the give command with the leading slash, and pressing Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback indicates that a trident was given, and one trident is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: If the trident is not already in the hotbar, press E to open the inventory and move the trident into any of the nine slots in the bottom hotbar row. Close the inventory with E or Esc. Select that hotbar slot using its number key, 1 through 9, or the mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: The trident is visible in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Confirm that the selected trident is not enchanted with Riptide. If necessary, open the inventory with E and hover the pointer over the trident to inspect its tooltip; the tooltip must not list Riptide. Close the inventory afterward without enchanting the item.
steps.success_cue: The selected test item is a trident with no Riptide enchantment.

steps.action: Return the crosshair to the open space chosen earlier while keeping the unenchanted trident selected.
steps.success_cue: The gameplay HUD is visible, the MC-278071 sidebar remains configured, and the player is holding the unenchanted trident while aiming into clear space.

steps.action: Press and hold the Use Item control, which is right mouse button by default, until the trident has completed enough of its draw-back animation to be thrown. Continue holding briefly rather than clicking and immediately releasing.
steps.success_cue: The player is visibly holding the trident in its charged throwing pose, ready for release.

steps.action: Release the Use Item control once to throw the trident. Do not press the attack control and do not make another throw.
steps.success_cue: The trident leaves the player's hand as a projectile, confirming that one unenchanted trident throw has occurred.

steps.action: Wait until the throwing animation has completed and normal player input is responsive. Do not retrieve, attack with, or throw the trident again. Leave the gameplay HUD visible briefly so the already-configured MC-278071 sidebar can be inspected before opening a menu.
steps.success_cue: The single throw is complete, no second trident use has occurred, and the MC-278071 sidebar remains displayed on the gameplay HUD.

steps.action: Press Esc to open the pause menu, then select Statistics.
steps.success_cue: The Statistics screen is open.

steps.action: Select the Items tab on the Statistics screen.
steps.success_cue: The item-statistics table is displayed.

steps.action: Locate the trident entry in the Items statistics table. Scroll through the table if necessary, using the trident item icon and its hover tooltip to identify the correct entry, and bring its used-statistic value into view. Do not perform any additional trident actions.
steps.success_cue: The trident entry and its usage-statistic field are visible in the Items tab, ready for the observation subsystem to evaluate.

stor.handoff_condition: Exactly one unenchanted trident has been thrown after configuring the MC-278071 objective, no additional trident use has occurred, and the Statistics screen's Items tab is open with the trident usage entry in view. The observation subsystem should now evaluate the captured sidebar state and the displayed trident statistic.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode. Survival mode is selected as a practical test environment, while commands are enabled solely to execute the supplied scoreboard setup and deterministically provide the trident.
The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, difficulty, or whether the test was originally performed in single-player or multiplayer; none appears necessary for the supplied reproduction.
The exact visual layout and sorting of the Items statistics table are not specified. The executor may need to scroll or hover over item icons to identify the trident entry.
The report says to give yourself a trident but does not prescribe an acquisition method. The /give @s minecraft:trident command is used as a deterministic practical implementation.

In a fresh world, a scoreboard objective backed by an automatically tracked statistic may show only its sidebar heading until the player has a score entry; an initially empty player list should not be treated as setup failure.
